biography.name: Noor

background.family: Lives with her father and older sister.
background.finances: Steady middle income; family would compare several education routes.
background.cultureLanguages: English and Urdu within the extended family.
background.school: Public high school with a school magazine and writing electives.
background.accessOpportunities: Library research and teacher editing support; limited portfolio experience outside school.

timeline.story: In 2014, Noor enjoyed listening to stories and correcting an adult who skipped a familiar sentence. She also liked sorting small toys into families, changing their relationships whenever a more interesting plot occurred to her.

At six, she began writing short accounts of ordinary afternoons. During 2017, she disliked a class dance performance and preferred helping write the introduction, though adults initially assumed all creative activities would appeal equally to her.

In 2018, Noor kept several unfinished stories in a folder and returned to revise their openings. She was more interested in finding the right sentence than illustrating the pages or turning the story into a performance.

During 2020, she spent free time rewriting fiction and checking details online when a story needed them. Technical demonstrations felt less engaging, while a quiet hour spent choosing between two words could hold her attention comfortably.

At twelve, Noor joined the school magazine and learned that factual articles required a different kind of checking. In 2023, she worked with a teacher to correct a piece whose appealing anecdote was not supported by its sources.

Across 2024 and 2025, she maintained several story drafts and edited magazine contributions. Music, acting, dance, and visual effects remained unappealing, and she disliked promotional tasks that required persuading classmates to care about a publication.

At sixteen in 2026, Noor is exploring Texas college writing courses and portfolio-based alternatives. She wants quiet autonomy and useful feedback, while remaining uncertain about how she would manage deadlines, outside expectations, and the less solitary parts of sustained writing work.
